raw_response:
I’m 65 this year, and I’ve farmed this land long enough to know cotton is not a crop you manage by guessing. On 15 mu, I can still handle it with my family, but I have to watch labor and cash. I usually stay with cotton because I know the field, the water situation, and the work rhythm. Since I have well irrigation, I’m not as exposed as dryland farmers, but pumping costs money, so I won’t water too freely. At the start of the season, my thinking is simple: keep the area in cotton, use a reliable improved variety, put enough base fertilizer so the stand starts strong, then add more later only if the crop is carrying well. I don’t chase extreme yield at my age. I want a steady crop, manageable labor, and no big mistakes. If the seedlings come up evenly and the summer rain is decent, I can expect a normal year. If pests rise, especially bollworm or aphids, I will spray when I see the problem instead of spraying blindly.
